reviews.label: A
strengths: Provides every required artifact: headline, subhead, five bullets, CTA, three FAQ answers, section order, developer checks and a primary measurement.
Arithmetic is largely accurate: CVR, ATC, checkout-start, Meta/Shopify mismatch, Daypack contribution margin and basic sample-size calculation.
Ties changes directly to the three support-ticket themes and correctly prioritizes mobile given the device split.
issues: Uses the 120 simulated review count as on-page social proof, which conflicts with the warning that the reviews are themes and not licensed testimonials.
Claims a 15-inch laptop may fit loosely in the main compartment without any supplied dimensions or fit confirmation.
Recommends a lifestyle first image without confirming the asset is available.
Some uncertainty is well handled, but the brief is overconfident on unverified laptop fit and social proof.
critical_errors: Treats simulated review data as usable review-count social proof.
Makes an unsupported 15-inch main-compartment fit statement.

output.summary: B and C are the strongest overall: both are complete, accurate, brand-appropriate, cautious about reviews and measurement, and operationally realistic. B edges C because its primary metric is closer to purchase conversion and its handling of laptop fit is especially restrained. D is also strong and quantitatively careful, but its before/after ATC target is less rigorous and it omits resource allocation. A has excellent structure and arithmetic, but it wrongly treats simulated review count as on-page proof and makes an unsupported 15-inch fit claim.
